'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Western Syria clashes (December 2024–present)|Western Syria clashes]]
***[[2025 massacres of Syrian Alawites]]
****The [[Syrian Observatory for Human Rights]] (SOHR) reports a marked re-escalation of [[Extrajudicial killing|extrajudicial killings]] of civilians in [[Alawites|Alawite]]-dominated coastal [[Syria|Syrian]] regions, with sixteen civilians executed in 72 hours. Several civilian homes in [[Tartus Governorate]] are seized by [[General Security Service (Syria)|government-affiliated forces]]. [https://www.syriahr.com/%d8%ae%d9%84%d8%a7%d9%84-48-%d8%b3%d8%a7%d8%b9%d8%a9-%d8%a7%d9%84%d9%85%d8%b1%d8%b5%d8%af-%d8%a7%d9%84%d8%b3%d9%88%d8%b1%d9%8a-%d9%8a%d9%88%d8%ab%d9%82-16-%d9%85%d8%af%d9%86%d9%8a%d8%a7-%d9%82%d8%aa/756214/ (SOHR)] [https://www.syriahr.com/%d8%a7%d8%b3%d8%aa%d8%a8%d8%a7%d8%ad%d8%a9-%d9%84%d8%ad%d9%82%d9%88%d9%82-%d8%a7%d9%84%d9%85%d9%88%d8%a7%d8%b7%d9%86%d9%8a%d9%86-%d8%a8%d8%b1%d9%8a%d9%81-%d8%b7%d8%b1%d8%b7%d9%88%d8%b3-%d8%b9%d9%85/756248/ (SOHR 2)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[War crimes in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***A video leaked by [[Government of Ukraine|Ukrainian officials]] and verified by the [[Associated Press]] shows [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian soldiers]] [[summary execution|summarily executing]] four [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[prisoners of war]] last month in [[Piatykhatky, Zaporizhzhia Oblast|Piatykhatky]], [[Zaporizhzhia Oblast]]. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-pows-war-crimes-putin-zelenskyy-4e834fb44b904d010d401563dbf4c5dc (AP)]
*[[Papua conflict]]
**Seventeen people are killed by [[West Papua National Liberation Army]] (TPNPB) militants in [[Yahukimo Regency]], [[Highland Papua]], [[Indonesia]]. The TPNPB alleges that they attacked [[Indonesian Army]] soldiers disguised as [[gold mining|gold miner]]s, while the [[Indonesian government]] rejects the claim. [https://apnews.com/article/indonesia-papua-rebels-gold-miners-52d3a76c7ac76d7862d6c047c9ef06de (AP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Tariffs in the second Trump administration]]
** [[China–United States trade war]]
***[[Executive Office of the President of the United States|The White House]] clarifies the [[tariff]] rate on [[China]], stating that a 145% tariff on all imports to the [[United States]] is in effect. The 20% addition came from China's alleged role in supplying [[synthetic opioids]], including [[fentanyl]], to the United States. [https://www.nytimes.com/2025/04/10/business/economy/china-tariffs-145-percent.html (''The New York Times'')]
**The [[European Union]] announces a 90-day pause on counter measures against the [[United States|U.S.]] [[tariff]]s on [[Economy of the European Union|European goods]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/cn4jjw30d5qt (BBC News)]
*[[Land reform in Zimbabwe]]
**[[Zimbabwe]] begins issuing the first [[financial compensation]] payments to [[White Zimbabweans|White Zimbabwean]] farmers whose farms were seized by [[Robert Mugabe]]'s government between 2000 and 2002. A total of 740 farmers will be compensated as per the 2020 agreement with the [[Commercial Farmers' Union]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq5wwp5eelxo (BBC News)]
*The [[United Kingdom]]'s [[Cabinet Office]] announces it will cut around 2,100 jobs from its department, about a third of its total workforce, as part of wider government [[austerity|spending cuts]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c62ggm3g8eyo (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 Hudson River helicopter crash]]
**A [[Bell 206]] sightseeing helicopter crashes into the [[Hudson River]] off [[Lower Manhattan]], [[New York (state)|New York]], United States, killing [[Siemens]] [[Spain]] CEO [[Agustín Escobar]], his family of four, and the pilot. [https://apnews.com/article/new-york-helicopter-crash-e0368ea529659ee1513d92dcbf05a28d (AP)] [https://abc7.com/post/helicopter-crashes-hudson-river-new-york-city/16153688/ (ABC News)]
*[[Jet Set nightclub roof collapse]]
**The number of deaths caused by the [[Structural integrity and failure|roof collapse]] of the Jet Set [[Nightclub|nightclub]] in [[Santo Domingo]], [[Dominican Republic]], rises to 221, as rescue operations reach the end. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/world/article/hope-of-finding-survivors-fades-in-aftermath-of-dominican-club-roof-collapse/ (CTV News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Hungary]]'s Minister of the [[Prime Minister of Hungary|Prime Minister]]'s Office [[Gergely Gulyás]] suggests a [[biological attack]] could be the source of a [[foot-and-mouth disease#Hungary_and_Slovakia_(2025)|foot-and-mouth disease outbreak]] in the country. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/hungary-investigating-outbreak-foot-and-mouth-disease-orbans-chief-staff-says-2025-04-10/ (Reuters)] 

'''International relations'''
*[[Russia–United States relations]]
**A [[Russian-American]] citizen arrested in [[Yekaterinburg]] in early 2024 and a [[Multiple citizenship|dual]] [[Russians in Germany|German-Russian]] citizen arrested in [[Cyprus]] in 2023 are released in a [[prisoner swap]] between [[Russia]] and the United States. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c0l005w2j86o (BBC News)]
*[[South Korea–Syria relations]]
**[[South Korea]] formally establishes [[diplomatic relations]] with [[Syria]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/south-korea-establishes-diplomatic-ties-with-syria-north-korea-ally-2025-04-10 (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2025 Turkish protests]]
**The [[government of Turkey]] releases 127 people on [[bail]], most of which are [[university student]]s, after they were arrested for taking part in protests calling for the release of [[Istanbul]] [[Mayor of Istanbul|mayor]] and [[Republican People's Party|opposition]] figure [[Ekrem İmamoğlu]]. [https://apnews.com/article/turkey-prisoners-students-protests-imamoglu-f4762e0faaa54ed3694fdc80b9a43edf (AP)]
**[[General Directorate of Security (Turkey)|Turkish police]] detain two [[journalist]]s, one from ''[[BirGün]]'' and one from ''[[Cumhuriyet]]'', and raid their offices, accusing them of [[intimidation|making threats]] and [[blackmail]] after they reported on the arrest of İmamoğlu. [[Reporters Without Borders]] condemn the arrests as an infringement on [[freedom of information]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/turkey-detains-two-journalists-in-ongoing-protests-againt-the-erdogan-government/a-72199916 (DW)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Presidency of Javier Milei]]
**[[Argentines]] organize a 24-hour [[Argentina|nationwide]] [[general strike]] against the [[Javier Milei]] [[Presidency of Javier Milei|administration]] for the third time. According to [[Government of Argentina|the government]], this constitutes an "attack against the republic". [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/argentine-workers-launch-widespread-24-hour-strike-against-mileis-austerity-measures (''The Straits Times'')] [https://uk.news.yahoo.com/argentina-strike-halts-trains-planes-203731056.html (Yahoo News)]
*The [[German governing coalition]] announces it will abolish the expedited 3-year [[German nationality law|naturalization path]] for "[[integration of immigrants|integrated]]" [[Immigration to Germany|immigrants]] who are spouses of [[Germans|German citizens]] or have completed the [[Integrationskurs]]. The path requiring 5 years of continuous [[permanent residency|residency]] will remain. [https://www.dw.com/en/new-german-coalition-to-abolish-3-year-citizenship-path/a-72202030 (DW)]
*[[Brigitte Haas]] is sworn in as the first female [[Prime Minister of Liechtenstein]]. [https://www.vaterland.li/liechtenstein/politik/neue-regierung-ist-im-amt-art-595778 (''Vaterland'')]
